samples.summary: `weights` is interpolated into the Google Fonts URL unencoded, and the new preview path now sources it from an untyped DOM attribute
samples.evidence: `familyParam()` builds `family=${encodeURIComponent(family)}:wght@${weights ?? DEFAULT_WEIGHTS}` — the family is percent-encoded but the weight spec is concatenated raw. Before this change the only values reaching that slot were typed `FontEntry.weights` fields from generated data. The change adds a second source: `ensurePreviewFontLink(family, text, weights)` is called from both observers with `row.dataset.fontWeights` (font-family-picker.tsx:152, more-fonts-dialog.tsx:154), i.e. a `string | undefined` read back out of the DOM. `previewWeight()` (font-catalog.ts:184) only splits on `;` and trims — it does not validate that the value is numeric — so a value containing `&` or `#` (e.g. `400&family=Foo` or `400#`) would append or truncate query parameters on the outbound third-party stylesheet request. Attack chain incomplete: I grepped the committed catalog data (`font-catalog.data.ts`, `font-catalog.full.ts`) for any `weights` value containing a character outside `[0-9;]` and found none, and the only writers of `data-font-weights` are the two components in this diff, so the value is not attacker-reachable today without pre-existing DOM write ability. The defect is that the sink lost its type guarantee while remaining unencoded — `encodeURIComponent` on the weight (or a `/^[0-9;.]+$/` check) closes it.

samples.summary: `hasFullFamilyLink` identifies the font provider by substring match on the whole href instead of by origin
samples.evidence: `if (!href.includes('fonts.googleapis.com')) continue;` treats ANY stylesheet URL that merely contains that string anywhere — path, query or fragment — as a Google Fonts request, e.g. `https://attacker.example/s.css?ref=fonts.googleapis.com&family=Inter`. Combined with the `[?&]family=…` scan two lines below (line 227), such a link makes `hasFullFamilyLink('Inter')` return true and permanently suppresses the preview request for that family. Impact is confined to preview suppression (a font renders in the fallback face); no data is exposed and nothing is executed. Reported because host-by-substring is the anti-pattern that becomes a real bypass the moment this helper is reused for a trust decision — `new URL(href).host === 'fonts.googleapis.com'` is the same cost. Reaching it also presupposes an attacker can already inject a `<link>`, so this is hardening, not an exploit.

samples.summary: New API forwards caller-supplied DOM text to a third-party host (`&text=`) with no constraint on what may be sent
samples.evidence: `ensurePreviewFontLink` puts `uniqueChars(text)` into the query of a request to `fonts.googleapis.com`, and both call sites feed it `row.textContent ?? ""` (font-family-picker.tsx:151, more-fonts-dialog.tsx:153). I traced every current caller: the picker rows render `entry?.label ?? family` where `family` comes from the `wafflebase:recent-fonts` localStorage list written only by `applyPick` (font-family-picker.tsx:180), and the dialog rows render label + group — so today only font names leave the browser, which the pre-existing `family=` parameter already disclosed. The residual concern is that the function's contract is now "hand me whatever this element paints and I will ship its characters to Google": any future row that inherits document text (a preview-text input, a 'fonts used in this document' section) would silently exfiltrate user content to a third party, and nothing in the function or its JSDoc bounds that. No leak is demonstrable on this branch, hence low confidence; a length/charset bound or a comment forbidding document-derived text would remove the trap.
searchedFor: grep addRecentFont|getRecentFonts across **/*.{ts,tsx} — only picker writes recents
read font-family-picker.tsx and more-fonts-dialog.tsx row markup for any document-derived text
grep for Content-Security-Policy in repo (no app-level CSP constrains the font host)
